system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The reported PowerShell activity is recorded at 13:42 UTC, shortly after the reported approximate time. It ran the organization’s documented workstation-patching command, with sam.okafor as the user.
The preceding network logon identifies sam.okafor and WS-SOKAFOR-01, the organization’s stated sole source for remote administration.
The PowerShell activity is followed by a Windows Update download through the proxy and execution of wusa.exe on a patch file, consistent with workstation patching.
PowerShell and wusa.exe both terminate shortly afterward.
The records also show connection attempts from DC-NWD-01 to WS-ICHEN-01 on ports 8080, 443, 445, and 135; the logged attempts on 8080, 443, and 445 were refused.

known_telemetry_limitations: The process records show the PowerShell command line but do not provide the script contents or a script hash, so the executed script’s contents cannot be independently verified from these records (T044-00084, T044-00085).

The DC-to-workstation connection attempts are recorded, but these records do not establish their purpose or show a successful connection (T044-00127, T044-00128, T044-00129, T044-00130, T044-00131, T044-00132, T044-00133, T044-00134).
claims_not_established: The available records do not independently establish who initiated the patching beyond the sam.okafor account attribution, or whether the activity was explicitly authorized at that moment (T044-00069, T044-00084, T044-00085).

The available records do not establish whether the DC-to-workstation connection attempts were related to the patching or to separate activity (T044-00127, T044-00128, T044-00129, T044-00130, T044-00131, T044-00132, T044-00133, T044-00134).
